Avoid timing your buys

While Palantir's growth prospects are compelling, its valuation already reflects extreme levels of optimism. The stock trades around 87 times forward earnings, leaving investors particularly vulnerable if results disappoint or guidance falls short of expectations.

While I see Palantir as an attractive artificial intelligence stock, investors should focus on the company's ability to sustain revenue growth, expand profitability, and strengthen its competitive moat over the next decade.

title: Palantir Trades at 150 Times, Josh Brown Says. Monday’s Guidance Has to Do More Than Beat
detail:
Palantir Trades at 150 Times, Josh Brown Says. Monday’s Guidance Has to Do More Than Beat
Gian Estrada
Fri, October 30, 2026 at 7:47 AM EDT 5 min read
PLTR
JPM

Trading disclosure
Palantir Trades at 150 Times, Josh Brown Says. Monday's Guidance Has to Do More Than Beat ©@Mungkhoodstudio's Images via Canva, @aukidphumsirichat via Canva
Key Takeaways

Palantir Technologies (PLTR:NASDAQ) reports third-quarter results on Monday, Nov. 2. Going in, Oppenheimer called for another revenue beat and guidance raise, and J.P. Morgan initiated coverage at Overweight with a $262 target.

Wall Street's 2026 revenue estimate is already above the top of Palantir's own guidance, so a beat and a routine raise are expected.

Since the end of June, Palantir's forward P/E has climbed from 74x to 103x, while next year's EPS consensus rose 13%.

The fourth-quarter guide is the number to watch, because it has to lift 2027 revenue and EPS estimates for the stock to grow into its multiple.

Palantir reports third-quarter results after the close on Monday, Nov. 2, and Wall Street has turned more bullish going in.

On Oct. 29, Oppenheimer said Palantir is set for another revenue beat and annual guidance raise. The same day, J.P. Morgan initiated coverage at Overweight with a $262 target for December 2027, about 33% above Wednesday's close.

Ritholtz Wealth Management CEO Josh Brown came at it from the price. On this week's episode of the Prof G Markets podcast, he argued that Anthropic looks reasonable next to the free cash flow it could produce. Then he made the comparison:

"Palantir is at 150 times."

At that price, beating the numbers is the easy part.

Brown didn't say which earnings he meant. His figure is close to Palantir's multiple on the past year's reported earnings. On forward estimates, Palantir trades at 103x, right on its five-year average:

PLTR Stock NTM P/E: 5-Year (TIKR)

That's well below the 270x peak of Oct. 31, 2025, but triple the 34x low of May 2022. And it has climbed back fast: it was 74x at the end of June.

TIKR Tracks 31 Analysts on Palantir. How Many Say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Palantir, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Palantir's Analyst Ratings

The Raise Is Already in the Numbers

Even the new bull's case rests on what comes after the quarter. J.P. Morgan analyst Brian Essex wrote: "Palantir is already delivering ROI by leveraging its platform to fundamentally transform the business operations of its customers, and growth is accelerating."

Palantir beats its own guidance as a habit, and by more each time: $76 million in the fourth quarter of 2025, $97 million in the first quarter and $134 million in the second. It raised its 2026 revenue guide in May and again in August, to $8.150 billion to $8.158 billion, or 82% growth.

Consensus already has 2026 revenue at $8.22 billion, above the top of that range:

PLTR Revenue: Actual and Consensus Estimates, 2023-2028 (TIKR)

The same goes for the quarter. Analysts expect $2.18 billion of third-quarter revenue, above the $2.160 billion to $2.164 billion Palantir guided.

Next year's $12.4 billion estimate is about 50% growth. That's about $3.1 billion a quarter. Palantir's current guidance implies roughly $2.4 billion for the fourth quarter.

Next Year's Earnings Have to Do the Lifting

Analysts expect normalized EPS of $1.61 this year and $2.35 in 2027:

PLTR Normalized EPS: Actual and Consensus Estimates, 2023-2028 (TIKR)

At the end of June, that 2027 figure was $2.08, so August's beat and raise and the revisions after it added 13%. Over the same stretch, the forward P/E went from 74x to 103x, up about 40%, roughly three times the move in 2027 estimates.

If the price holds, a 13% rise in the next 12 months' EPS estimates would take the forward multiple from 103x to about 91x. A token raise barely moves it.

What Monday Has to Show

Palantir has rarely traded on estimate math. A hot U.S. commercial number or a big government contract could swing the stock more than any revision. But next year's estimates are built on those same numbers:

U.S. commercial revenue: $764 million in the second quarter, up 149%. Monday's figure laps $397 million from last year's third quarter, and the full-year guide is at least $3.424 billion (134% growth).

Total remaining deal value: up 83% to $13.1 billion in the second quarter. That's slower than revenue's 93% and down from 105% growth at the end of 2025.

The fourth-quarter revenue guide: against the roughly $2.4 billion the current outlook implies.

The third-quarter expense line will matter for margins, but revenue guidance is what drives the 2027 estimates.

A beat and another full-year raise are already expected, with consensus revenue above management's guidance, so a raise that only covers this year does little for a 103x multiple. Palantir needs a fourth-quarter guide well above $2.4 billion, and remaining deal value growing faster again, to push 2027 estimates up by double digits the way August's report did.

Full 2027 guidance won't come until the fourth-quarter report in early February, so Monday can only start that work.

title: Could $1,000 Invested in Palantir Turn Into $100,000?
detail:
Could $1,000 Invested in Palantir Turn Into $100,000?
Leo Sun, The Motley Fool
Thu, October 29, 2026 at 4:50 PM EDT 4 min read
PLTR
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Palantir (NASDAQ: PLTR) went public via a direct listing on Sept. 30, 2020. A $1,000 investment at its earliest trading price of $10 would be worth about $19,400 today. That's an impressive six-year gain, but could it eventually turn that investment into $100,000?

How fast is Palantir growing?

Palantir operates two data-gathering platforms: Gotham for government clients, and Foundry for commercial clients. These platforms create digital twins of a client's entire organization by collecting data from their databases, supply chain reports, sensors, internal documents, emails, financial records, social media accounts, and other disparate sources.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

Palantir then uses its data model, Ontology, to unify that fragmented data into an easy-to-query stream of information for non-technical users. Its clients can connect that data to third-party software and large language models (including OpenAI's ChatGPT and Anthropic's Claude) via its Artificial Intelligence Platform (AIP) to make faster data-driven decisions. Its top customers include major defense and intelligence agencies, as well as commercial giants like Walmart, Amazon, and ExxonMobil.

From 2021 to 2025, Palantir's revenue grew at a 31% CAGR. It also turned profitable in 2023 and grew its EPS at a 165% CAGR over the following two years. The intensifying geopolitical conflicts drove the U.S. government to award more contracts to Palantir, and the growth of the AI market tethered more commercial customers (especially in the U.S.) to its platform.

From 2025 to 2028, analysts expect Palantir's revenue and EPS to grow at CAGRs of 59% and 70%, respectively. That growth should be fueled by the expansion of the enterprise AI market, new defense modernization contracts, and the monetization of AIP with subscription modules. However, its stock isn't cheap at 91 times next year's earnings.

Could Palantir turn $1,000 into $100,000?

Palantir's near-term future looks bright, but it probably can't maintain those breakneck growth rates. If it matches analysts' estimates through 2028 and continues to grow its EPS at an impressive 30% CAGR over the following 13 years, its EPS would reach $94.19 by 2041. At 50 times forward earnings, its stock would be trading at $4,710 in 2040.
